name: Body Scan Meditation
description: Systematic attention to body sensations combined with breath awareness.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Lie down comfortably on your back."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Close eyes and take 3 deep breaths."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Bring attention to your feet. Notice sensations."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Slowly move attention up: legs, hips, belly, chest."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Continue to arms, hands, neck, face, head."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "If you find tension, breathe into that area."}]
safety_warning: If you feel dizzy, panicky, or emotionally overwhelmed, open your eyes, return attention to the room, and stop. Avoid lying flat if it worsens reflux, breathing issues, or back pain; choose a supported position instead.
history: Core MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) practice developed by Jon Kabat-Zinn.
tips: ["Don't try to change anything, just notice","It's okay to fall asleep","Do before bed"]

name: Cold Exposure
description: Brief cold exposure activates the vagus nerve and builds stress resilience.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "At the end of your regular shower, prepare mentally for cold water."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Take a deep breath and turn the water to cold."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Start with 30 seconds of cold water on your body."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Focus on slow, controlled breathing."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Gradually increase duration over days/weeks up to 2-3 minutes."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "End with the cold water and step out feeling invigorated."}]
safety_warning: Avoid if you have heart conditions, Raynauds disease, or are pregnant. Start gradually and never force yourself.
history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
tips: ["Find a quiet, comfortable place","Practice regularly for best results","Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable"]

name: Ear Massage
description: Stimulate vagus nerve branches in the ear through gentle massage.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Sit comfortably and take a few deep breaths."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Gently massage your earlobes between thumb and forefinger."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Move up along the outer edge of your ear, massaging gently."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Press gently into the hollow behind your earlobe."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Massage the inner folds of your ear with light pressure."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Finish by gently pulling your earlobes downward 3 times."}]
safety_warning: Use light pressure only. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, ringing in the ears, or nausea. Avoid massaging over infection, open skin, recent piercing, or recent ear surgery; seek medical advice if unsure.
history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
tips: ["Find a quiet, comfortable place","Practice regularly for best results","Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable"]

name: Eye Movement Exercise
description: Gentle eye movements that stimulate the vagus nerve and reduce stress.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Lie on your back comfortably."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Interlace fingers behind your head."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Without moving your head, look to the right."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Hold for 30-60 seconds until you sigh or yawn."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Return to center, then look left."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Hold again until you sigh, swallow, or yawn."}]
safety_warning: Stop if you feel dizziness, nausea, headache, or eye pain. Avoid if you have a recent concussion, eye surgery, or a condition where eye strain worsens symptoms unless cleared by a clinician.
history: Based on Stanley Rosenberg's work on the vagus nerve and cranial nerves.
tips: ["A sigh or yawn means it's working","Keep head still","Can do seated too"]

name: Gargling
description: Simple gargling activates muscles connected to the vagus nerve.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Fill a glass with water."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Take a sip of water."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Tilt head back and gargle vigorously."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Continue until you need to breathe."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Spit out and repeat."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Do this for 1-2 minutes daily."}]
safety_warning: Do not gargle if you have trouble swallowing or are at risk of choking. Use small sips and stop if you cough, choke, or feel short of breath. Avoid tilting your head far back if it causes dizziness or neck pain.
history: The muscles used in gargling are innervated by the vagus nerve.
benefits: ["Tones vagus nerve","Easy daily practice","Improves gag reflex"]
tips: ["Do it while brushing teeth","Gargle until eyes water slightly","Twice daily is ideal"]

name: Grounding Moment
description: Quick sensory awareness exercise to bring you back to the present.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Notice 5 things you can see."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Notice 4 things you can touch."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Notice 3 things you can hear."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Take 2 deep breaths."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Name 1 thing you are grateful for."}]
safety_warning: If deep breaths make you lightheaded, switch to normal breathing and do the sensory steps only. If you feel unsafe or overwhelmed, pause and seek support.
history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
tips: ["Find a quiet, comfortable place","Practice regularly for best results","Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable"]

name: Heart 7 - Shen Men
description: Acupressure on the "Spirit Gate" point. Calms the heart, reduces anxiety, and promotes peaceful sleep.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Find the crease on the inside of your wrist."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Locate the point on the pinky side of the crease."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Press gently with thumb, hold for 30 seconds."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Breathe deeply while pressing."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Switch to other wrist and repeat."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Do 3 rounds on each wrist."}]
safety_warning: Press gently—do not cause pain, numbness, or tingling. Avoid acupressure over broken/irritated skin or recent wrist injury. Stop if you feel dizzy or unwell.
history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
tips: ["Find a quiet, comfortable place","Practice regularly for best results","Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable"]

name: Humming / OM Chanting
description: Vibrations from humming stimulate the vagus nerve through the larynx.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Sit comfortably with your spine straight."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Take a deep breath in through your nose."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "As you exhale, make a humming sound (like mmmmm) or chant OM."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Feel the vibration in your throat, chest, and head."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Continue for the duration, taking natural breaths between hums."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Experiment with different pitches to find what feels most resonant."}]
safety_warning: Keep breathing comfortable—do not strain or force long exhalations. Stop if you feel lightheaded, short of breath, or throat discomfort. If you have asthma/COPD or voice issues, keep it gentle and consult a clinician if symptoms worsen.

tips: ["The vibration directly stimulates your vagus nerve","Lower pitches create stronger vibrations","Great for anxiety and before sleep"]

name: Khoomei Breathing
description: Mongolian throat singing breathing technique for deep vibration and meditation.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Sit comfortably with spine straight."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Take a deep breath filling belly completely."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Begin a low drone sound from deep in throat."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Shape mouth to create different overtone harmonics."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Feel vibrations in chest, throat, and head."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Continue for 10-15 minutes, experimenting with sounds."}]
safety_warning: Start gently to avoid straining throat.

benefits: ["Deep vibration therapy","Voice strengthening","Unique meditation","Vagus nerve stimulation"]
tips: ["Start with simple humming","Drink water before and after","The sound matters less than the vibration"]

name: Military Sleep Method
description: Technique used by military to fall asleep in 2 minutes or less.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Lie down and relax your entire face, including tongue and jaw."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Drop your shoulders and let arms hang loose."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Exhale and relax your chest."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Relax your legs from thighs down to feet."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Clear your mind for 10 seconds. Think 'don't think'."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Picture yourself in a calm place, or repeat 'don't think'."}]
safety_warning: If you feel anxious, panicky, or uncomfortable while lying down, switch to a supported position or stop. Do not use this technique while driving or when you need to stay alert.

name: Pericardium 6 - Nei Guan
description: The "Inner Gate" point relieves nausea, anxiety, and calms the heart. Used for motion sickness too.

name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
description: Systematically tense and release muscle groups to release physical tension.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Lie down comfortably. Take 3 deep breaths."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Squeeze your feet tightly for 5 seconds, then release."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Move to calves: squeeze 5 seconds, release."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Continue up: thighs, glutes, belly, chest, hands, arms."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Squeeze face muscles, then release completely."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Finally, tense entire body at once, then let go."}]
safety_warning: Stop if you feel pain, cramping, tingling, or dizziness. Avoid forcefully tensing any injured or recently operated areas; keep contractions gentle and breathe normally.
history: Developed by Edmund Jacobson in the 1920s for anxiety and tension relief.
tips: ["Squeeze at 70% intensity, not max","Notice the contrast after releasing","Great before bed"]

name: Vocal Toning
description: Use your voice to create vibrations that stimulate the vagus nerve.
instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Sit or stand comfortably."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Take a deep breath in."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "On exhale, make a long 'OOOOMMM' or 'AAAHHH' sound."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Feel the vibration in your chest and throat."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Experiment with different pitches."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Continue for 3-5 minutes."}]
safety_warning: Keep the volume comfortable and do not strain your voice. Stop if you feel lightheaded, throat pain, or shortness of breath; people with voice/throat conditions should use gentle humming or consult a clinician.
history: Vocal vibrations have been used across cultures to induce calm and connection.
tips: ["Lower pitches create stronger chest vibrations","Don't strain your voice","Hum if you prefer"]

name: Voluntary Yawning
description: Yawning activates the vagus nerve and releases tension in the jaw and face.

name: Yoga Nidra

instructions: [{"step": 1, "instruction": "Lie in Savasana (corpse pose) with eyes closed."}, {"step": 2, "instruction": "Set a Sankalpa (positive intention/resolve)."}, {"step": 3, "instruction": "Rotate awareness through body parts systematically."}, {"step": 4, "instruction": "Observe breath without changing it."}, {"step": 5, "instruction": "Visualize peaceful images or scenes."}, {"step": 6, "instruction": "Return to Sankalpa, then slowly wake up."}]
